messages:
nina park: hey all, first day! trying to run the onboarding pipeline but Buildkite can't checkout the repo. error shows a 403 on git fetch. any quick tips?

kevin zhao: welcome nina :) can you paste the build link and the exact checkout error? also are you using a fork or a branch on the org repo?

nina park: https://buildkite.com/redwood/onboarding/builds/90
Checkout error:
```
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood/my-service.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403
```

infra-bot: Reminder: Buildkite checkout uses the GitHub App installation token by default. A 403 usually means the app isn't installed on the repo or SSO blocked the installation for your user/org.

kevin zhao: another possible cause: repo was switched to use a deploy key or changed from HTTPS to SSH in Buildkite settings and the pipeline doesn't have the right creds.

nina park: i accepted the GitHub App invite yesterday, and i can clone the repo locally with my PAT. i did push my branch to the org.

luis mendoza: two things i check: (1) repo-level app install: org -> settings -> installed GitHub Apps -> make sure Redwood CI shows green for that repo; (2) Buildkite project settings -> repository access method (App vs SSH key).

kevin zhao: nina, can you confirm the pipeline's settings page shows "Connected with GitHub App"? sometimes during migration it flips to "Repository deploy key" and the key might be expired.

nina park: pipeline shows "Connected via: GitHub App"

infra-bot: Tip: If the GitHub App is installed but SSO requires approval, the app's installation token won't have access until an org admin approves SSO for the app. Check GitHub org -> SSO -> Approved Applications.

kevin zhao: also check the Buildkite project's repository URL matches the org/repo case-sensitively. We had a case where a dot/uppercase mismatch caused webhook and checkout failures.

nina park: i can't view org SSO approvals or the app install page (no perms yet).

luis mendoza: ok i'll check infra side. meanwhile, if you need to unblock CI you can either: (A) ask infra to trigger a manual build using a machine user token we keep in ops, or (B) run the local onboarding script (./dev/ci/run-local.sh) to validate steps.

(luis checks infra)
luis mendoza: infra confirms the app was installed but SSO approval is pending for "redwood-ci-bot". until an admin approves, the installation token returns 403 for protected repos. infra will ping the org admins now.

kevin zhao: thanks @luis. nina, try triggering a manual Buildkite run via the UI (if you have pipeline access) while infra escalates — sometimes the manual trigger uses cached credentials and works, but if it's SSO-blocked it will still 403.

nina park: i don't have Trigger permission yet. if infra can escalate that would be huge.

(luis pings admins)

(5 minutes later)
luis mendoza: admin approved SSO for the CI app. infra re-synced installation tokens. could you re-run or push a trivial commit to retrigger?

nina park: pushed a tiny whitespace change to my branch. build started and checkout succeeded! :tada:

kevin zhao: nice. i'll add a one-liner to the onboarding doc: if checkout 403 -> check GH App install + SSO approval + Buildkite repo access method (App vs deploy key) and pipeline permissions.

nina park: super helpful, thanks everyone. excited to be here!"
